recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-26677; future RequestStatus changes should be reconciled under their own Jira keys across the value set, Request pattern text, and state-machine diagram.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive R5 technical correction reporting that the Request Pattern Request.status definition and state-machine wording used values that did not match the bound Request Status value set expansion, particularly suspended/cancelled versus on-hold/revoked.
initial_application: Jira cites git master 2ed04c432f777fa8be8e47a7596c8c36dc0ac434. That commit updated source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml and the Request state-machine diagram sources to replace the stale suspended/cancelled Request status wording with on-hold/revoked alignment.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists request as an active logical pattern, making the inspected source/request files and Request state-machine image current-build evidence. Later FHIR-48861 added ended as a RequestStatus parent for completed/revoked and is already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-20563, also already represented on the combined branch, cleaned up related suspended/cancelled wording in request-derived resources. The originating Zulip workflow thread confirms the tracker came from the same value-set-versus-definition mismatch and no Confluence evidence was found that changes the conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/request/codesystem-request-status.xml, source/request/valueset-request-status.xml, source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml, source/request/request-spreadsheet-notes.xml, and images/request-state-machine.svg are aligned: Request.status lists the current RequestStatus codes including on-hold, ended, completed, and revoked, while the state-machine labels use on-hold and revoked rather than suspended/cancelled.
